According to the WTO director, stablecoins accounted for roughly 3 percent of global payments in 2026.

Fragmented regulatory regimes across jurisdictions hinder broader integration of stablecoins into international finance, the organization said.

The director said trade-finance operations could see reduced friction if licensing rules converge.

Adoption remains limited, with officials pointing to uneven oversight in several markets.

The WTO did not publish a new binding standard alongside the remarks.

Member governments were told that licensing remains national rather than a single WTO-wide rule.

The director cited 2026 payment-share data rather than a forecast for later years.

Officials said no enforcement timetable accompanied the comments.
